key_insight: Motile microorganisms can self-organize into bioconvective flows that passively enhance heat and mass transfer, offering a bio-inspired route to low-energy thermal management.
engineering_relevance: Bioconvection could be integrated into hybrid cooling systems to reduce pumping power, weaken thermal boundary layers, and improve heat-transfer efficiency for data centers and other energy-intensive technologies.
method: Reviewed natural and laboratory studies of microorganism-driven hydrodynamics and pattern formation
Synthesized thermofluidic transport mechanisms relevant to bioconvective heat transfer
Interpreted performance using key non-dimensional numbers
evidence_signal: The abstract reports quantitative analyses of thermal performance across bioconvective systems, supporting the feasibility assessment with thermofluidic metrics rather than only qualitative observations.
watch_item: Practical deployment remains constrained by microbial stability, material compatibility, controllability, scalability, and integration with existing cooling hardware.
paper_title: Engineering Collective Microbial Dynamics for Sustainable Thermal Management
